name: EoH (Evolution of Heuristics)
org: City University of Hong Kong, Huawei Noah's Ark Lab, Southern University of Science and Technology
one_liner: An LLM writes each heuristic as a short idea in words plus code, and both evolve together under performance-based selection.

loop.proposes: Heuristics as a natural-language 'thought' plus code, made by five LLM prompt operators
loop.judged_by: Running the code on benchmark instances and measuring fitness
loop.steers: Fitness drives selection of parents for the next generation of a fixed-size population

headline_result: On online bin packing, EoH with about 2,000 LLM queries (GPT-3.5-turbo) averaged a 1.18% gap to the lower bound over six test sets, against 2.23% for FunSearch (which the paper says needs around 1 million queries), 4.13% for best fit and 4.51% for first fit. It also reached the best-known tour on three TSPLib instances (pr124, kroA150, u159) and led on Taillard flow-shop sets.
caveat: Main experiments use GPT-3.5-turbo on three classic problems. Comparisons are on the authors' own set-ups, and FunSearch's query count is quoted from its published runs, not re-run.
beyond_harness_note: The evolutionary loop is the solver over a population, and the output is a heuristic that runs without any model.
generative_model: Pretrained LLM, frozen (GPT-3.5-turbo in main runs; Gemini Pro, CodeLlama, DeepSeek compared)
algorithmic_authority: Benchmark evaluation of the heuristic code

sources.title: Evolution of Heuristics: Towards Efficient Automatic Algorithm Design Using Large Language Model

verification.notes: Resolved arXiv:2401.02051 (Liu, Tong, Yuan, Lin, Wang, Lu, Zhang; v1 4 Jan 2024; v3 1 Jun 2024). Numbers from Table 9 and text via the HTML version. Draft claim 'beats hand heuristics incl. online bin packing' holds. I could not confirm a conference venue from arXiv metadata, so none is stated.
